title: Rotate the vCenter automation secret while its in-flight requests drain
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. The vCenter automation service account is past its rotation window. Last night's attempt signed in again on the new secret and dropped the previous session immediately, which killed everything that was still open on it; the operator found out from a half-applied change rather than from the rotation job. Rebuild it properly.

Build a Python package `vcfrotate` at the workspace root, runnable as `python3 -m vcfrotate`. It rotates that account's vCenter session over the vSphere Automation API and hands the workload from the retiring session to the incoming one without abandoning anything that is already in flight.

Use the Python standard library only: `urllib.request` is the transport. Do not take a third-party HTTP or VMware dependency (`requests`, `httpx`, `pyvmomi`, `vsphere-automation-sdk`), do not vendor one, and do not shell out to `curl`.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not from a documentation page, and not from the 9.1 revision of that same file. It names the only four operations in scope, `Cis.Session_create`, `Cis.Session_get`, `Cis.Session_delete` and `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue`, and for each one it carries the server base path, method, path, security scheme, request body media type and schema, and success status, alongside the `wireRules` that say how a request has to be shaped. Take every property name and value set from that file. The acceptance harness may point `--contract` at a copy that serves the same operations under a different server base path, so resolve each request from the contract instead of hard-coding URLs.

Command line:

`python3 -m vcfrotate --base-url <url> --username <user> --old-password <pass> --new-password <pass> --work <path> --report <path> [--contract <path>] [--workers <int>]`

`--contract` defaults to `docs/contract.json` and `--workers` to 4.

The work file is a JSON object holding two arrays, `in_flight` and `post_rotation`. Every element has an `id` and a `subject_token_type`, and may also set any of `resource`, `audience`, `scope`, `requested_token_type`, `actor_token` and `actor_token_type`. One element is one `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue` call. `in_flight` is the work that is already open when the rotation starts; `post_rotation` is the work that arrives once the new secret is live.

Requirements:

- Open the retiring session with `Cis.Session_create` over HTTP Basic using `--old-password`, then dispatch every `in_flight` element against that session concurrently, at most `--workers` at a time.
- Rotate alongside that work rather than behind it: while the in-flight exchanges are still open, open the incoming session with `Cis.Session_create` and `--new-password`, then call `Cis.Session_get` exactly once, on the incoming session, and confirm the `user` it reports is `--username`.
- Only once every in-flight exchange has settled may the retiring session be terminated with `Cis.Session_delete`. Then run the `post_rotation` elements on the incoming session, again concurrently, and release the incoming session with `Cis.Session_delete` last.
- An abort has to leave the retiring session alive so the rotation can be retried, and has to let the in-flight work finish anyway. If the first login is refused, `aborted_reason` is `login_failed`. If `--new-password` is refused, drain and stop, and `aborted_reason` is `new_session_rejected`. If the incoming session reports a different principal, drain, terminate the incoming session and stop, and `aborted_reason` is `user_mismatch`. Never terminate the retiring session on any of those paths.
- The session identifier `Cis.Session_create` returns travels in the `vmware-api-session-id` header of every later call, and those calls carry no `Authorization` header. `Cis.Session_create` carries the Basic credentials and no session header. The three operations that declare no request body must send none and must not declare a `Content-Type`.
- `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue` sends `Vcenter.Authentication.Token.IssueSpec` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. `grant_type` is the token-exchange URN the contract pins, `subject_token_type` comes from the work element, and `subject_token` is the standard base64 encoding, with padding, of the session identifier that request is bound to, as the specification's own note on that property requires. Every optional property the element did not set must be absent from the body rather than sent with an empty value, and every property that is sent appears exactly once.
- `--report` receives a JSON object with exactly the keys `user`, `outcome`, `aborted_reason`, `retired_session_deleted` and `requests`. `user` is the principal `Cis.Session_get` reported, or null when it was never called. `outcome` is `rotated` when the retiring session was terminated and `aborted` otherwise. `aborted_reason` is null on a clean rotation. `requests` lists every work element, the `in_flight` ones first and each group in work-file order, as an object with `id`, `phase` (`in_flight` or `post_rotation`) and `status`.
- A `status` of `succeeded` also carries `issued_token_type`, read out of the endpoint's `Oauth2.TokenInfo`. A `status` of `failed` instead carries `error` with exactly `http_status`, `error` and `error_description`, read out of the endpoint's own response: for an `Oauth2.Errors.Error` that is its `error` and `error_description`, and for a vAPI error it is `error_type` and the default text of the first localizable message. An element that never ran is `not_attempted` and carries neither.
- Exit 0 when the outcome is `rotated` and nothing failed, and exit 1 otherwise. Write the report on both paths. Never print or store either password.

Acceptance: `python3 -B verify.py`. It boots a contract-pinned loopback vCenter on `127.0.0.1` with dummy credentials, holds the in-flight token exchanges open so the rotation genuinely overlaps them, and drives the job through a clean rotation, both refused-login paths, a mismatched principal, and failed exchanges using both documented endpoint error shapes. It then reads the mock's request log to assert the exact method, target, session binding, credential placement, form body property set, the omission of every unset optional property, the configured concurrency ceiling, report schemas, and the ordering that proves the retiring session outlived its own in-flight work. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.py`, `mock_vcenter.py`, `.gitignore` and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
